                                    50.5.2                         SPI error flags
              Mode fault (MODF)
              Mode fault occurs when the master device has its internal slave select logic input (NSS pin 
              in slave select hardware mode, or SSI bit in slave select software mode) pulled low. This 
              automatically affects the SPI interface in the following ways:
              •  The MODF bit is set and the interrupt request is triggered if the MODFIE bit is set.
              •  The SPE bit is forced to zero while MODF bit is set. This blocks all the peripheral 
                 outputs and disables the SPI interface.
              •  The MASTER bit is cleared, thus forcing the device into slave mode.
              MODF is cleared by writing 1 to the MODFC bit in the SPI_IFCR. 
              To avoid any multiple slave conflicts in a system comprising several MCUs, the NSS pin 
              must be pulled to its non-active level before re-enabling the SPI, by setting the SPE bit. 
              As a security, hardware does not allow the SPE bit to be set while the MODF bit is set. In a 
        2184/3329              RM0433 Rev 9
